rationale: The last interpretation's counterevidence said the configuration events only exercised a configured-but-absent participant (the black-hole stepper), so this turn replaced it with a real one. The sweep now builds four state machines (ids 1..4) whose storage ConfState is voters {1,2,3}, wraps only 1..3 with newNetwork and registers node 4 directly in the network's peer map, because newNetwork rewrites the trackers of every peer it is given (it would otherwise make all four nodes voters up front and hide the configuration change under test). Node 4 therefore starts outside the configuration but answers: when a ConfChange adds it, the leader replicates to a peer that processes messages, and the persist/apply loop (which now iterates over 1..4) hands committed conf changes to applyConfChange on node 4 as well, so it can be a learner, a voter, or be removed and re-added. The invariant checks (at-most-one-leader-per-term, committed (index,term) consistency, committed-index monotonicity, applied<=committed) now also cover node 4 and its committed index. Draft-side run of this revision reports invariant_sweep_summary with seeds=60, steps_per_seed=60, elections=460, ordinary proposals=461, conf_change_proposals=335 and violations=0, i.e. still no witness with a participating configured node. That is construction feedback only, so the experiment below requests isolated execution of these bytes; joint-transition proposals and restarts are still not part of the event set, so the gap stays open.

scope.description: Fifth revision of the same fixed harness; probes A, B and C are unchanged. The sweep case now uses four real state machines: ids 1..4 are built with newTestRaft(id,10,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2,3))) so their stored configuration is voters {1,2,3}; the network wraps 1..3 through newNetwork (whose peer branch would otherwise install all four as voters) and node 4 is registered directly in the network peer map as a real raft instance. A ConfChange event proposes one change on node 4 (AddLearnerNode, AddNode or RemoveNode) through confChangeToMsg/MsgProp on the current leader; the persist/apply step iterates over ids 1..4, applying every committed EntryConfChangeV2 through applyConfChange, so node 4's own configuration changes when it applies its log. Event mix, invariant checks and the summary event (seeds, steps, elections, ordinary proposals, conf_change_proposals, violations) are otherwise unchanged; configurations remain simple changes, with no joint transition, and node restarts are still absent.
assumptions: Everything comes from the snapshot's own test facilities (newTestRaft, newTestMemoryStorage, withPeers, newNetwork, nextEnts, confChangeToMsg, applyConfChange); no production logic is modified.
Node 4 begins outside its own configuration (its storage ConfState is voters {1,2,3}), which is the state a joining node has before it applies the configuration change that adds it.
The three operations proposed for node 4 are safe to apply repeatedly, so the random sequence cannot drive the configuration into an invalid transition.
Randomness is fixed per seed; absence of violations is a holds-only result for this event set, not a safety proof.

experiment.prefix: For each of 60 seeds: build nodes 1..4 with newTestRaft(id,10,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2,3))); nt := newNetwork(nodes[1],nodes[2],nodes[3]) so that the trackers used by the protocol are voters {1,2,3}, then nt.peers[4] = nodes[4] so node 4 is reachable by the network but starts outside the configuration. Then for 60 steps pick one of MsgHup on a random node, MsgProp with a tagged payload, tick() on a random node, isolate a random node, recover, TransferLeader from a random voter to the current leader, a ConfChangeV2 proposal on the leader (AddLearnerNode/AddNode/RemoveNode for node 4), or persist/apply of all nodes; after each step persist/apply nodes 1..4 (applying committed conf changes through applyConfChange) and evaluate the four invariants, emitting a violation event with seed, step, nodes and operands when one is found, and finally emitting invariant_sweep_summary.
experiment.revision_reason: Same investigation and same sweep case as the previous execution, with the configured participant made real: node 4 is now a reachable raft instance that starts outside the configuration instead of the package's black-hole stepper, the apply loop covers node 4, and the stored ConfState is pinned to voters {1,2,3}. Fresh execution is requested because the harness bytes and the event set changed.
